# OHZI Core — LLM Reference

## What is OHZI Core?

OHZI Core is a TypeScript WebGL/WebGPU graphics library built on top of [Three.js](https://threejs.org/). It is **not meant to be used standalone** — it is part of the [OHZI Boilerplate](https://github.com/ohzinteractive/boilerplate), which provides the full project scaffolding.

The library ships as an ES module (`build/index.mjs`) with TypeScript declarations (`types/index.d.ts`). It wraps and extends Three.js with a structured framework for:

- Application lifecycle management
- Rendering pipeline control (render modes, post-processing)
- Scene and camera management
- Asset loading and caching
- Viewport and timing utilities
- Input handling
- Debug visualization

All classes are exported from the top-level package. Import them directly:

```ts
import { Graphics, RenderLoop, Time, OScreen, SceneManager, CameraManager, BaseApplication } from '@ohzi/core';
```

---

## Core Concepts

### Singletons vs Instantiable Classes

Many core systems are **singletons** — exported as a single shared instance, created when the module loads. `Initializer.init()` initializes most of them once at startup. `Graphics` needs its own `Graphics.init()` (see below), and `TransitionManager`, `ViewManager`, `ViewComponentManager`, `MeshSampler` and `ModelUtilities` need no init.

Singletons: `Graphics`, `Time`, `OScreen`, `SceneManager`, `CameraManager`, `CameraUtilities`, `ResourceContainer`, `Debug`, `OS`, `Browser`, `Capabilities`, `TransitionManager`, `ViewManager`, `ViewComponentManager`, `MeshSampler`, `ModelUtilities`.

Instantiable: `BaseApplication`, `PerspectiveCamera`, `OrthographicCamera`, `KeyboardInput`, `RenderLoop`, `AbstractScene` (subclasses), and all materials, loaders, components, etc.

### Application Startup Sequence

```ts
// 1. Initialize all core singletons
Initializer.init(input);

// 2. Initialize the renderer (separate because it needs a DOM element and DPR)
Graphics.init({ renderer, core_attributes, dpr: window.devicePixelRatio });

// 3. Create camera and assign it
const camera = new PerspectiveCamera(60, OScreen.aspect_ratio, 0.1, 1000);
CameraManager.current = camera;

// 4. Set a render mode
Graphics.set_state(new NormalRender());

// 5. Create and start the render loop with your application
const app = new MyApplication();
const loop = new RenderLoop(app, Graphics, input);
loop.start();
```

### Teardown

```ts
Initializer.dispose(loop);
// This calls: Graphics.dispose() → SceneManager.dispose() → loop.dispose()
```

---

## RenderLoop

The central frame driver. It calls lifecycle hooks on a `BaseApplication` instance every frame.

```ts
const loop = new RenderLoop(app, Graphics, input);
loop.start();   // begins requestAnimationFrame via renderer.setAnimationLoop
loop.stop();    // calls app.on_exit(), detaches animation loop
loop.dispose(); // stop + reset frame counter (allows full restart)
loop.set_state(newApp); // swap apps mid-run (calls on_exit/on_enter)
```

**Frame order each tick:**

1. `Time.__update()` — update delta/elapsed
2. `app.on_post_start()` — called once on frame 2
3. `input.update()` — process raw events
4. `app.before_update()`
5. Fixed-timestep loop: `app.fixed_update()` (0–N times)
6. `Time.__set_frame_interpolation()`
7. `app.update()`
8. `app.on_pre_render()`
9. `Graphics.update()` — main scene render
10. `app.on_post_render()`
11. `Debug.render()` — debug overlay
12. `app.on_frame_end()`
13. `input.clear()` / `Debug.clear()`

---

## BaseApplication

Extend this to implement your application logic. All methods are no-ops by default.

```ts
class MyApp extends BaseApplication
{
  on_enter(loop: RenderLoop)
  {
    // Called once when this app becomes active
  }

  update()
  {
    // Called every frame after fixed updates
    // Use Time.dt for frame-rate-independent movement
  }

  fixed_update()
  {
    // Called at a fixed rate (default: 30 Hz)
    // Good for physics and deterministic logic
  }

  on_pre_render()  { /* before Graphics renders */ }
  on_post_render() { /* after Graphics renders */ }
  on_frame_end()   { /* very end of frame */ }
  on_exit(loop)    { /* cleanup when leaving this state */ }
}
```

---

## Graphics

Singleton that wraps the Three.js WebGPU `Renderer`. Manages rendering, post-processing, resize, and screenshots.

```ts
// Render a scene manually
Graphics.render(scene, camera, renderTarget, overrideMaterial);

// Full-screen post-process blit pass
Graphics.blit(srcRT, dstRT, material);
Graphics.material_pass(mat, dstRT);

// Switch render mode (e.g., NormalRender → UnrealBloomRender)
Graphics.set_state(new UnrealBloomRender());

// Screenshot (tiled, high-res)
Graphics.take_screenshot((blob) => Graphics.download_screenshot(blob), 3840, 2160);

// Read back GPU pixels to CPU
const pixels = await Graphics.readback_RT(renderTarget);
```

**Key properties:**

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `Graphics._renderer` | The raw Three.js `Renderer` instance |
| `Graphics.canvas` | The `HTMLCanvasElement` |
| `Graphics.current_render_mode` | The active `BaseRender` instance |
| `Graphics.blitter` | `Blitter` for blit passes |
| `Graphics.depth_and_normals_renderer` | Generates depth/normal G-buffer |
| `Graphics.generate_depth_normal_texture` | Set `true` to enable depth/normal pass each frame |

---

## Render Modes

Render modes are classes extending `BaseRender` that control how the scene is drawn each frame. Switch between them via `Graphics.set_state()`, which calls `on_exit(Graphics, renderer)` on the old mode and `on_enter(Graphics, renderer)` on the new one. Until then `Graphics.current_render_mode` is `Graphics.no_render`, a plain `BaseRender` that draws nothing.

`BaseRender` hooks (all empty in the base class):

| Method | Called by |
|--------|-----------|
| `render()` | `Graphics.update()` each frame when `CameraManager.current` is set, and `Graphics.take_screenshot()` once per tile |
| `on_enter(context, renderer)` / `on_exit(context, renderer)` | `Graphics.set_state()`. `context` is `Graphics` |
| `dispose()` | `Graphics.dispose()`, on the active mode only. No built-in mode overrides it |
| `resize()` | Nothing in core. Modes resize their render targets at the start of `render()` to match `OScreen` |

Available render modes:

| Class | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `NormalRender` | Standard clear → render pipeline. Calls the scene's `on_pre_render()`, `render()` and `on_post_render()` |
| `BloomRender` | Box blur bloom. `new BloomRender(use_dual_filtering = false)`: `true` blurs with `DualFilteringBlurrer` for a much wider glow. Builds its targets in `on_enter()` and frees them in `on_exit()` |
| `UnrealBloomRender` | Unreal-style bloom: five Gaussian mips summed with per-mip tints, added over the scene. `new UnrealBloomRender(use_antialiasing, use_half_float, use_hight_luminosity_pass, use_rendering_size = false)`: the first three are required. Tune with `set_bloom_strength()`, `set_bloom_radius()`, `set_luminosity_threshold()` (only with the high pass) and `set_tint_color_0()`…`set_tint_color_4()` |
| `NormalAORender` | Normal + AO pass. `new NormalAORender(use_ssaa = false, use_exact_depth = true)`: `use_ssaa` renders the scene at 2×; turning `use_exact_depth` off roughly halves the SSAO pass cost but bands flat surfaces |
| `DeferredRender` | Deferred point lights over `Graphics.depth_normals_RT`. The constructor fills `scene_lights` with a 2×2 grid of demo lights; edit it to place your own |
| `VRRender` | For WebXR (`core_attributes.xr_enabled: true`). Three's XR manager renders the stereo views; the mode does not clear, and `render_spectator_camera()` mirrors the headset view to the canvas when `CameraManager.spectator` is set |
| `DebugNormalsRender` | Visualize world-space normals with a `NormalMaterial` override |

Only `NormalRender` and `VRRender` run the scene's render hooks. The other modes call `Graphics.render(SceneManager.current, ...)` directly, so `on_pre_render()` and `on_post_render()` overrides do not run under them.

`NormalAORender` and `DeferredRender` set `Graphics.generate_depth_normal_texture = true` in `on_enter()` and never reset it. Set it back to `false` when switching to a mode that does not need the depth and normals pass.

`BloomRender`, `UnrealBloomRender`, `NormalAORender`, `DeferredRender` and `DebugNormalsRender` use TSL materials and run on `WebGPURenderer` with both its WebGPU and WebGL2 backends.

Custom render modes extend `BaseRender` and implement `render()`:

```ts
class MyRender extends BaseRender
{
  render()
  {
    Graphics.clear(undefined, CameraManager.current, true, true);
    SceneManager.current.on_pre_render();
    SceneManager.current.render();
    // post-process: Graphics.blit(srcRT, dstRT, myMaterial)
    SceneManager.current.on_post_render();
  }
}
```

---

## Time

Singleton for all frame-timing values. Read in `update()` or `fixed_update()`.

```ts
Time.dt            // delta_time in seconds (current frame)
Time.sdt           // smooth_delta_time (10-frame rolling average)
Time.elapsed_time  // total seconds since app start
Time.frame_interpolation // 0–1 fraction between fixed steps (use for visual interpolation)
Time.fixed_delta_time    // fixed step interval, default 1/30 s (writable)
```

---

## OScreen

Singleton for viewport/canvas dimensions and DPR. Updated automatically by `Graphics` on resize.

```ts
OScreen.width          // CSS logical width
OScreen.height         // CSS logical height
OScreen.render_width   // physical pixels (width * dpr)
OScreen.render_height  // physical pixels (height * dpr)
OScreen.aspect_ratio   // width / height
OScreen.dpr            // device pixel ratio
OScreen.pixel_size     // Vector2(1/width, 1/height) — useful in shaders
OScreen.size_changed   // true for one frame when a resize occurred
OScreen.portrait       // true when width < height
```

---

## SceneManager

Singleton holding the active Three.js scene.

```ts
SceneManager.current = myScene; // set active scene
SceneManager.current;           // read active scene
SceneManager.dispose();         // dispose all geometries/materials in current scene
```

The rendering pipeline (`NormalRender`, etc.) always reads `SceneManager.current` as the default scene.

---

## CameraManager

Singleton holding the active camera.

```ts
CameraManager.current = new PerspectiveCamera(60, OScreen.aspect_ratio, 0.1, 1000);
CameraManager.current;   // read active camera
CameraManager.spectator; // secondary VR spectator camera
```

`Graphics.update()` syncs `CameraManager.current.aspect` to `OScreen.aspect_ratio` automatically each frame.

---

## PerspectiveCamera / OrthographicCamera

Thin extensions of their Three.js counterparts adding `clear_color` and `clear_alpha` per camera.

```ts
const cam = new PerspectiveCamera(60, OScreen.aspect_ratio, 0.1, 1000);
cam.clear_color = new Color('#1a1a2e');
cam.clear_alpha = 1;
CameraManager.current = cam;
```

---

## CameraController

Not a singleton — one per scene, usually in `AbstractScene.camera_controller`. An orbital rig around `reference_position`, at `reference_rotation` (from tilt and orientation in degrees: positive tilt looks down, orientation turns counterclockwise about +Y) and `reference_zoom` (a distance, clamped to `[min_zoom, max_zoom]`).

```ts
class OrbitState extends CommonCameraState
{
  update(cc: CameraController)
  {
    super.update(cc);            // tracks W/A/S/D, Z/C
    this.__move_camera(cc);      // keys + right drag pan
    this.__zoom_camera(cc);      // wheel
    this.__rotate_camera(cc);    // left drag, with inertia
  }
}

const cc = new CameraController(Input);
cc.set_camera(camera);
cc.set_state(new OrbitState(Input));
cc.set_rotation(30, 45);         // tilt, orientation; call before the first update()
cc.focus_on_bounding_box(box, 0.8);

// Each frame (not called automatically):
cc.update();                     // state.update → mode.update → update_normalized_zoom
```

- The default mode is `ImmediateMode`: it copies `reference_rotation` to the camera and places it `reference_zoom` behind `reference_position`. `set_camera()` does not sync `reference_rotation` from the camera.
- Rotation: `set_rotation(tilt?, orientation?, azimuth?)`, `set_rotation_delta()`, `set_quaternion()`, `lerp_tilt()`, `lerp_orientation()`, `lerp_rotation()`, `lerp_quaternion()`. Azimuth is stored but never applied; `lerp_azimuth()` is empty.
- Framing: `focus_camera_on_points()`, `focus_on_bounding_box()`, `focus_camera_on_sphere()`; `fit_points()`, `get_zoom_to_focus_on_points()` and `get_target_pos_to_focus_on_points()` compute without applying. Orthographic cameras frame through `camera.zoom`. A scale above 1 frames tighter.
- `normalized_zoom` is recomputed from the camera distance on every `update()` (1 at `min_zoom`, 0 at `max_zoom`), so `set_normalized_zoom()` does not last.
- `enable()` / `disable()` only set `input_enabled`; `CommonCameraState` ignores it.

See `docs/CameraController.md` for the full API.

---

## CameraFitting

`CameraUtilities` is a singleton instance, initialized by `Initializer.init(input)`. `PerspectiveFrustumPointFitter` and `OrthographicFrustumPointFitter` are instantiated; `CameraUtilities` and `CameraController` use them for framing.

```ts
// Frame a box for the camera's current rotation; nothing is applied
const fit = CameraUtilities.fit_bounding_box_points(camera, box, 0.9);   // below 1 leaves a margin
camera.position.copy(fit.camera_position);
if (camera.isOrthographicCamera)
{
  camera.zoom = fit.zoom;                // orthographic cameras frame through zoom
  camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
}

// The point under the mouse (input.NDC) on the ground plane
const point = CameraUtilities.get_plane_intersection(new Vector3(), new Vector3(0, 1, 0));

// World position → canvas pixels, origin top left
const pos = CameraUtilities.get_html_screen_pos(object, camera);
```

- `fit_points(camera, points, zoom_scale)` returns `{ zoom, reference_position, camera_position }`. `zoom` is a distance for perspective and `camera.zoom` for orthographic. A `zoom_scale` above 1 frames tighter.
- `fit_points_on_camera(points, zoom_scale)` uses `CameraManager.current` and returns `{ position, zoom }`. Its `zoom_scale` scales the area to fit, so above 1 leaves a margin, the opposite of `fit_points`.
- The perspective fit uses `camera.aspect`, not `OScreen.aspect_ratio`. The orthographic fit keeps the camera's distance when the points' depth fits between the near and far planes.
- `get_plane_intersection` returns `(0, 0, 0)` when the ray misses the plane. `unproject_mouse_position` works with perspective cameras only.
- `update_projection(camera)` sizes an orthographic camera to `OScreen` pixels.
- `FrustumPointFitter` is an unused copy of `PerspectiveFrustumPointFitter` that logs to the console on every fit.

See `docs/CameraFitting.md` for the full API.

---

## AbstractScene

Abstract base class for scenes. Extend it to define assets, setup logic, and per-frame hooks. Implements a **two-phase loading pipeline**: regular quality → high quality.

```ts
class MyScene extends AbstractScene
{
  constructor()
  {
    super({ name: 'my_scene', compilators: { SceneCompilator, TexturesCompilator, AudiosCompilator } });
    this.set_assets(sceneObjects, sceneTextures, sceneSounds);
    this.set_high_assets(hqObjects, hqTextures, []);
  }

  init()
  {
    super.init();
    // One-time setup: add lights, meshes, etc.
  }

  on_assets_ready()
  {
    // Regular assets downloaded — access via ResourceContainer.get('name')
  }

  on_assets_compiled()
  {
    super.on_assets_compiled(); // required: triggers high-quality load
    // Assets compiled and GPU-ready
  }

  on_high_quality_assets_ready()
  {
    // High-quality assets done
  }

  on_pre_render()
  {
    // Update uniforms, animate objects, etc.
  }
}
```

**Loading flow:** `scene.load()` → a shared web worker downloads the assets and the main thread decodes them → `on_assets_ready()` → compilators run (spread across frames) → `on_assets_compiled()` → high-quality load starts → `on_high_quality_assets_ready()`.

**State flags:**

| Property | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `scene.is_loaded` | Regular assets compiled and ready |
| `scene.is_high_loaded` | High-quality assets loaded |
| `scene.loading_progress` | 0–1 loading progress |

---

## ResourceContainer

Singleton asset cache. A resource stored for a URL is reused by later loads of that URL, but two loads of one URL that start before either finishes both download.

```ts
// Write (done automatically by loaders)
ResourceContainer.set_resource('hero_tex', '/assets/hero.png', loadedTexture);

// Read (use in on_assets_ready / on_assets_compiled)
const tex = ResourceContainer.get('hero_tex');
```

Two different names pointing to the same URL resolve to the same object instance.

---

## Asset Loaders

### Batch async loaders (used by AbstractScene)

`AsyncObjectsLoader`, `AsyncTexturesLoader`, `AsyncAudiosLoader` — load arrays of asset descriptors. A shared web worker downloads them.

They extend `AsyncAbstractLoader(name, assets, worker)`. The worker comes from `AsyncAbstractLoader.create_worker()` and is stored as `ResourceContainer.set_resource('assets_worker', ...)`; `LoadingState` passes the scene name as `name`. The worker only downloads each asset into a blob URL. The main thread then decodes it with the resource loaders that `__setup_loaders()` returns. `load()` loads every loader that shares a `name`; poll `is_loaded()` and `get_progress()`.

| Class | Descriptor fields (plus `name`, `url`, `size`) | Creates |
|-------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| `AsyncObjectsLoader` | `draco` | `GLTFDRACOLoader` (with `ResourceContainer.get('draco_loader')`) or `GLTFLoader` |
| `AsyncTexturesLoader` | `kind`: `'regular'`, `'basis'`, `'hdr'`, `'cubemap'`, `'cubemap_hdr'`; `flipY`, `premultiplyAlpha`, `colorSpaceConversion`, `extension` | The matching texture loader. Other kinds are skipped |
| `AsyncAudiosLoader` | `loop`, `volume` (defaults to 0), `positional` | `AudioLoader` |

The worker doesn't report download progress, and a failed download means `is_loaded()` never returns `true`. `TextureLoader` and `VideoLoader` need the fetch response, so they can't be used inside an async loader.

### ResourceBatch

Runs loaders on the main thread, for example in the preloader:

```ts
const batch = new ResourceBatch('general_loader');
batch.add_loader(new JSONLoader('config', '/data/config.json', 2000));
batch.load(); // defaults to the ResourceContainer singleton

// Poll each frame
if (batch.loading_finished && !batch.has_errors) { const config = ResourceContainer.get('config'); }
```

Also: `get_progress()` (0–1), `get_loaded_bytes()`, `get_total_bytes()`, `print_errors()`.

### Individual loaders

All extend `AbstractLoader`. Construct one with `(resource_id, url, ..., size)`, call `load(resource_container)` (it returns nothing), then poll `has_finished` / `has_error`:

| Loader | Asset type |
|--------|-----------|
| `GLTFLoader` | `.gltf` / `.glb` |
| `GLTFDRACOLoader` | DRACO-compressed GLTF |
| `TextureLoader` | Images |
| `AsyncTextureLoader` | Images (async, via ImageBitmap) |
| `HDRTextureLoader` | `.hdr` equirectangular |
| `HDRCubeTextureLoader` | HDR cubemaps |
| `CubemapLoader` | Regular cubemaps |
| `BasisLoader` | Compressed textures through the loader passed in (the boilerplate passes a `KTX2Loader`) |
| `AudioLoader` | Audio files |
| `FontLoader` | Three.js JSON fonts |
| `OBJLoader` | `.obj` meshes |
| `DAELoader` | Collada `.dae` |
| `VideoLoader` | Object URL (`string`) for the video blob, not a texture |
| `FileLoader` | Raw file fetch |
| `TextLoader` | Text files |
| `JSONLoader` | JSON files |
| `PointArrayLoader` | Newline separated x, y, z values → `Vector3[]` |

---

## Materials

### Writing a material

Core materials are TSL node materials for `WebGPURenderer`. Full screen passes extend `BlitNodeMaterial`: `Blitter` sets `_MainTex`, `_Resolution` and `_TargetResolution`, and `sample_main_tex()` / `sample()` sample render targets and regular textures upright on both backends. Other materials extend `NodeMaterial` from `three/webgpu`. Keep uniforms under `this.uniforms.<name>` so callers can set `.value`.

```ts
import { Texture } from 'three';
import { texture } from 'three/tsl';
import { BlitNodeMaterial } from 'ohzi-core';

class AddTextureMaterial extends BlitNodeMaterial
{
  constructor()
  {
    super();

    const second_tex = texture(new Texture());
    this.uniforms._SecondTex = second_tex;

    this.fragmentNode = this.sample_main_tex().add(this.sample(second_tex));
  }
}
```

### Built-in materials

`AddMaterial`, `BlitNodeMaterial`, `UnrealBloomComposeMaterial`, `DualFilteringBlurMaterial` — ready-to-use post-processing materials.

| Material | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `BlitNodeMaterial` | Base of every full screen pass. Outputs `_MainTex` unchanged; depth test, depth write and blending are off. `sample_main_tex(offset?)`, `sample(texture_node, offset?)`, `uv_for()` and `texture_uv_at()` flip render targets so both kinds of texture come out upright |
| `AddMaterial` | `_MainTex + _SecondTex`, alpha included. `set_add_texture(tex)`, then `Graphics.blit(src, dst, add_mat)`. `new AddMaterial(use_half_float = false)`: the flag is ignored |
| `UnrealBloomComposeMaterial` | `new UnrealBloomComposeMaterial(nMips, use_linear_color_space = false)` (the flag is ignored). Sums `blurTexture1..N`, each times its tint and `mix(f, 1.2 - f, bloomRadius)` with `f = [1.0, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2]`, times `bloomStrength`. Reads no `_MainTex`, so run it with `Graphics.material_pass()`. `set_blur_texture_0()`…`_4()`, `set_tint_color_0()`…`_4()`, `set_bloom_strength()`, `set_bloom_radius()` (both default `1`); the numbered setters assume five mips |
| `DualFilteringBlurMaterial` | `new DualFilteringBlurMaterial(upsample)`: one dual filtering pass, 5 taps down or 8 taps up, offsets in half source texels from `_Resolution`, so drive it with `Graphics.blit()` |

---

## Render Utilities

None of the blurrers is a singleton. `Blurrer` and `DualFilteringBlurrer` blur in place and have `dispose()`. `GaussianBlurrer` writes its five mips (each at half the previous size, kernel radii `[3, 5, 7, 9, 11]`) to `renderTargetsVertical`, tunes with `set_radius()` and `set_luminosity_threshold()` (default `0.23`), and frees with `dispose_RT()` and `dispose_materials()`. `Blurrer` and `DualFilteringBlurrer` use 8-bit `RenderTarget` defaults for their internal targets.

```ts
// 9 tap separable blur at the input's size, in place
const box = new Blurrer();
box.blur(render_target);

// Dual-filter blur (efficient, large radius), in place
const blurrer = new DualFilteringBlurrer();
blurrer.blur(render_target);

// Gaussian blur: five mips, optional luminosity high pass, RT left unchanged
const gaussian = new GaussianBlurrer();
gaussian.set_radius(1.5);
gaussian.blur(render_target, true);
const widest_mip = gaussian.renderTargetsVertical[4].texture;

// Depth + normals G-buffer
Graphics.generate_depth_normal_texture = true;
// Access via: Graphics.depth_normals_RT
```

---

## Components

Ready-to-use Three.js `Object3D` subclasses:

| Class | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Grid` | 100 × 100 unit ground grid on XZ, a line every unit |
| `Line` | Line through 3D points |
| `Text2D` | Canvas text on a `WorldImage` plane in world space |
| `WorldImage` | Image plane in world space; faces the camera when `screen_aligned` (off by default) |
| `SDFTextBatch` | GPU-batched SDF text rendering |
| `UpdatableMaterialMesh` | Mesh with a per-frame material update hook |

```ts
// Thick polyline (needs 2+ points); a new point count replaces line.geometry
const line = new Line([new Vector3(0, 0, 0), new Vector3(1, 1, 0)]);
line.thickness = 0.05;                   // world units, default 0.2
line.color = '#00ffcc';

// Image plane, 1 unit tall; pivot -1..1, (0, 0) is the center
const image = new WorldImage(texture, new Vector2(0, -1));
image.screen_aligned = true;             // faces the camera, still sized in world units
image.size = new Vector3(2, 2, 2);       // sets the scale; the getter returns world width/height
image.update_texture();                  // after the texture's image changes

// Canvas text: color is a CSS string, the plane is 1 unit tall at any font size
const label = new Text2D('Hello', 'bold 48px Arial', '#ffffff', new Vector2());
label.text = 'Bye';                      // redraws; the getter returns 'not implemented'

// MSDF text: one instanced draw per batch, up to 2000 glyphs
const batch = new SDFTextBatch(font_layout, atlas_texture); // msdf-atlas-gen JSON, yOrigin: bottom
const text = batch.add_text('OHZI');     // SDFText; needs at least one drawable glyph
text.set_position(new Vector3(0, 2, 0)); // the batch's own transform is ignored
text.set_size(0.5);                      // 1 em = 1 world unit at size 1
batch.update();                          // every frame, or after any change
```

- `Line`, `WorldImage`, `Text2D` and `SDFTextBatch` render transparent with `depthWrite` off and ignore scene fog.
- `WorldImage.dispose()` also disposes its texture and throws when the image has no parent.
- Assign `SDFText` transforms through its setters; changing `position`, `quaternion` or `scale` directly does not mark it dirty. Its pivot moves the text by half its size per unit, the opposite sign of the `WorldImage` pivot.
- `UpdatableMaterialMesh` calls `material.update()` in `onBeforeRender` when the material has one; material arrays are skipped.

See `docs/Components.md` for the full API.

---

## CanvasDrawer

Not singletons — instantiate as needed. `CanvasDrawer` owns an offscreen canvas and leaves the drawing to `__draw()`; `SimpleTextDrawer` draws one line of text on a canvas sized to fit it.

```ts
const drawer = new SimpleTextDrawer();
const options = { font: 'bold 48px Arial', font_color: '#ffffff' }; // textAlign defaults to 'center'

const texture = drawer.draw_on_texture('Score: 0', options); // new CanvasTexture over drawer.canvas
texture.colorSpace = SRGBColorSpace;                         // render the CSS color as given
texture.needsUpdate = true;

drawer.draw_canvas('Score: 10', options);                    // redraws the same canvas
texture.needsUpdate = true;
```

- Every call draws into the same `canvas`, so textures from earlier `draw_on_texture()` calls show the new content after their next upload.
- `draw_canvas()` writes the `font` (`'24px Arial'`) and `font_color` (`'#000000'`) defaults into the options object you pass.
- `draw_on_texture()` uses nearest filtering, clamp to edge and no mipmaps, and sets no color space.
- The font height is measured once and cached unless `uses_dynamic_font` is `true`; `SimpleTextDrawer` takes no constructor arguments, so set the property after construction.
- `font_color` must be a CSS color string: a number is not a valid canvas color and the text stays black. A `textAlign` other than `'center'` draws at `x = 0`, so `'right'` and `'end'` end up off the canvas.

See `docs/CanvasDrawer.md` for the full API.

---

## Primitives

```ts
new Cube(size?, segments?, color?)                       // size and segments are Vector3
new Sphere(radius?, color?)                              // always 64 x 64 segments
new Arrow(color?, length?, dir?)                         // starts at its position
new HorizontalPlane(width?, height?, color?, material?)
new VerticalPlane(width?, height?, color?, material?)
```

- Every primitive is a `Mesh` with an unlit `MeshBasicMaterial`, red by default, and adds no methods or `dispose()`.
- `Arrow` starts at its origin and points along +Z, or along `dir` (normalized). Its `length` property reads and writes `scale.z`, a factor on the constructor length.
- `Arrow`, `HorizontalPlane` and `VerticalPlane` default the color with `||`, so a numeric `0` becomes red; `Cube` and `Sphere` use `??`.
- `HorizontalPlane` lies on XZ facing +Y, `VerticalPlane` on XY facing +Z. Both take an optional `material` that replaces the default one.
- `Sphere.center` is its `position`, so a `Sphere` can be passed to `CameraController.focus_camera_on_sphere()`. Its `radius` and `color` fields do not update the mesh.

See `docs/Primitives.md` for the full API.

---

## KeyboardInput

Not a singleton — instantiate as needed.

```ts
const kb = new KeyboardInput();
kb.init(document);
kb.register_key('Space');
kb.register_key('KeyW');

// In update():
if (kb.is_key_pressed('Space'))   { /* triggered once on press */ }
if (kb.is_key_down('KeyW'))       { /* true while held */ }
if (kb.is_key_released('Space'))  { /* triggered once on release */ }

kb.dispose(); // remove listeners
```

---

## Debug

Singleton for development-time overlays. All 3D objects added to a separate debug scene rendered after the main scene. Helpers stay until removed: `clear()` only clears the 2D canvas, not the 3D helpers.

```ts
// 3D debug shapes (drawn in debug scene)
Debug.draw_arrow(origin, direction, color);
Debug.draw_line([p1, p2, p3], color);
Debug.draw_cube(position, size, color);
Debug.draw_sphere(position, radius, color);
Debug.draw_axis();
Debug.draw_texture(renderTarget.texture, width, height);

// 2D overlay (requires Debug.ctx set to a CanvasRenderingContext2D)
Debug.draw_rectangle(pos2d, width, height, color);
Debug.draw_line_2D(from, to, color);
```

---

## RenderLayers

Named constants for Three.js layer indices:

```ts
RenderLayers.opaque       // 0 — default opaque geometry
RenderLayers.transparent  // 1 — transparent geometry
RenderLayers.outline      // 2 — outline-effect objects
RenderLayers.selectable   // 3 — raycasting-selectable objects

mesh.layers.set(RenderLayers.transparent);
camera.layers.enable(RenderLayers.opaque);
```

---

## OS / Browser / Capabilities

Singletons for platform detection, initialized by `Initializer.init()`. `OS` sets its flags right away; `Browser` sets most of its values a little later (see below).

```ts
OS.is_mobile   // true on phones/tablets
OS.is_ios      // true on iPhone/iPad
OS.is_android  // true on Android
OS.is_mac      // true on macOS
OS.is_windows  // true on Windows

Browser.is_chrome
Browser.is_firefox
Browser.is_safari
Browser.is_edge_chromium
Browser.name                      // 'chrome' | 'firefox' | 'safari' | 'edge_chromium' | 'edge_ie' | 'opera' | 'iexplorer' | 'other'
Browser.version                   // major version (Safari can be fractional, e.g. 17.4)
Browser.is_vr                     // WebXR supports 'immersive-vr'
Browser.preferred_video_extension // 'webm' | 'hvec.mp4' | 'mp4'

Capabilities.max_anisotropy                   // always 0 (never filled)
Capabilities.vertex_texture_sampler_available // always false (never filled)
```

`Browser.init()` is async: `name`, `version` and `is_vr` are set after the WebXR `isSessionSupported()` check resolves, and `Initializer.init()` does not await it. Every iOS browser detects as `safari`. `Capabilities` only has `max_anisotropy` (always `0`) and `vertex_texture_sampler_available` (always `false`); the `Graphics.init()` lines that would fill them are commented out. See docs/Browser.md.

---

## ActionSequencer

Event sequencing with interpolators — useful for scripted animations and transitions.

An `ActionSequencer` animates the keys of a context object. It makes one channel per key, and every key needs at least one interpolator. Times are in seconds.

```ts
const state = { fade: 0, height: 0 };
const seq = new ActionSequencer(state);

// add_action_interpolator(from_time, to_time, interpolator)
seq.add_action_interpolator(0, 1, new NumberInterpolator('fade', 0, 1, false, 'ease_in_out_cubic'));
seq.add_action_interpolator(0.5, 2, new NumberInterpolator('height', 0, 2));

// Calls window.ViewApi.application.home_view.play_intro('fast') at 1s
seq.add_action_event(1, new ActionEvent('home_view', 'play_intro', 'fast'));

// Each frame
seq.update(Time.delta_time); // writes state.fade and state.height
if (seq.is_finished()) { /* done */ }
```

Also: `play()`, `stop()`, `reset()`, `skip()`, `get_progress()` (0–1), `set_progress(seconds)`, `set_normalized_progress(t)`. `VectorInterpolator` has no `evaluate()`, so the sequencer can't play it.

- `add_action_interpolator(from, to, interpolator, true)` starts the keyframe from the previous keyframe's end value (or the key's initial value). Add a channel's keyframes in time order.
- `update()` writes values at the previous frame's time, so they trail by one frame; call `update()` once more after `is_finished()` to land on the final values. `skip()` jumps to the end without firing the events it passes.
- Per channel queries on the current keyframe: `get_current_starting_value(name)`, `get_current_target_value(name)`, `get_current_progress(name)` (eased), `is_channel_redefined(name)` (no default return track). `set_initial_value_on_channel()` / `set_final_value_on_channel()` override the first start and last end values.
- Easing names are `EasingFunctions` methods (`'linear'`, `'ease_in_out_cubic'`, ...). An unknown name throws when played.
- `ActionEvent` args are a comma separated string and every argument arrives as a string. `trigger()` throws without `args`.

`new ActionSequencerBuilder(default_state_data).from_animation_sheet(data, context)` is how `TransitionTable` builds transitions: one `NumberInterpolator` per track starting from the current value, one `ActionEvent` per trigger, plus tracks returning untouched default keys to their defaults. It pushes those tracks into `data.animation_tracks`. `from_draw_io(xml, context)` reads a draw.io timeline through `DrawIOAnimationSheet.parse(xml)` (100 px = 1 s; rectangles labelled `key=value--easing` are tracks, rhombi labelled `name.method` are triggers, without args).

See `docs/ActionSequencer.md` for the full API.

---

## View / UI System

`ViewManager`, `ViewComponentManager`, and `ApplicationView` provide a UI layer abstraction above Three.js, with transition animations driven by `TransitionManager`. These are wired into the `RenderLoop` automatically and updated each frame.

`ViewManager`, `ViewComponentManager` and `TransitionManager` are created when the module loads; `Initializer` does not touch them. `TransitionTable` lives in `TransitionManager.transition_table`.

### State data

`TransitionManager.current_state_data` is a flat object of numbers. Every frame, each view and view component copies its `<name>_opacity` key into its container's `style.opacity`. Set the defaults once at startup with `TransitionManager.set_default_state_data({ home_opacity: 0, ... })`. Every key a transition animates, or that you write, must be in them, or the next transition throws.

### ApplicationView

Extend it per page: `super({ name, url, container, transition_data? })`. The constructor registers the view with `ViewManager` and adds `{ to: name, data: transition_data }` to the transition table. Hooks:

- `before_enter()` / `before_exit()`: the transition starts. `on_enter()` / `on_exit()`: it ends (`on_exit()` also runs when another `go_to_view` interrupts it). The base class toggles the `before_enter`, `before_exit` and `hidden` classes on `container`, so call `super`.
- `update_enter_transition(state_data, progress, action_sequencer)` / `update_exit_transition(...)`: every frame of the transition, `progress` 0–1.
- `update()`: every frame while current and not transitioning. `before_update()` / `fixed_update()` run even during transitions.
- `start()`: never called by core; the app calls it.

### Navigation

```ts
ViewManager.go_to_view('about');              // change_url = true: pushState(url), title "ABOUT | <suffix>"
ViewManager.go_to_view('home', false, true);  // no URL change, skip the animation
ViewManager.go_to_scene('about');             // through the view named 'transition' (needs set_next_view(view))
ViewManager.set_view('home');                 // make current, no transition, no hooks
```

Also: `get(name)`, `get_by_url(url)`, `has_view(name)`, `get_current_view()`, `set_browser_title_suffix(suffix)`. `get()` returns `undefined` for an unknown name, and `go_to_view()` then throws. `get_view_by_name()` is deprecated and returns nothing.

### Transition data

`TransitionTable.get(from, to, context)` uses the entry matching both names, else the one with that `to` and no `from`, and builds an `ActionSequencer` over the state data. Add pair specific entries with `TransitionManager.add_transitions([{ from: 'home', to: 'about', data }])`; `set_transitions()` replaces the table, including the entries the views registered.

```json
{
  "animation_tracks": [
    { "attribute_name": "home_opacity", "from_time": 0, "to_time": 1, "to_value": 1, "easing_function": "ease_in_out_cubic" }
  ],
  "triggers": [{ "at_time": 0.5, "name": "home_view", "method": "play_intro", "args": "fast" }]
}
```

Times are in seconds (scaled by the `?transitions_velocity=` URL parameter). Default keys the data does not animate return to their default value over `min(longest track, 1)` seconds, so entering a view fades the other `*_opacity` keys out on their own. Triggers call `window.ViewApi.application[name][method](...args.split(','))`, and `args` is required.

### ViewComponent

UI outside the views (modals, overlays): `new ViewComponent({ name, container })` registers with `ViewComponentManager`. When `<name>_opacity` rises above 0.001 it calls `on_enter()` (removes `hidden`), and when it drops back it calls `on_exit()` (adds `hidden`). In between, `ViewComponentManager` calls `update(state_data)` every frame. `ViewComponentManager.get(name)` finds one; `get_component_by_name()` is deprecated and returns nothing.

See `docs/Views.md` for the full API.

---

## Utilities

Static helpers, except `MeshSampler` and `ModelUtilities` (singleton instances) and `TimeUtilities` / `CSSAnimator` (instantiate them).

```ts
OMath.lerp(a, b, t);
OMath.linear_map(value, 0, 1, -1, 1);   // not clamped
OMath.pingpong(t);                       // 0 → 1 → 0 as t grows
EasingFunctions.ease_in_out_cubic(t);    // method names double as easing strings in transition data

ModelUtilities.get_object(gltf.scene, 'Body');                    // last match by name
ModelUtilities.assign_material(gltf.scene, material, undefined);  // undefined name = every mesh
const copy = ModelUtilities.clone_animated_gltf(gltf);            // { animations, scene } with its own skeletons

const { points, normals, uvs } = MeshSampler.sample(mesh.geometry, 500);

HTMLUtilities.load_images(container);    // data-src → src for <img> and <object>

const fade = new CSSAnimator({ element, css_property: 'opacity', duration: 0.5 });
fade.animate();
fade.update();                           // every frame; advances by Time.delta_time
```

- `MeshSampler.sample` needs an indexed geometry, and it never returns if a triangle has zero area.
- `ModelUtilities.get_mesh` and `get_geometries` replace each mesh's geometry with a clone.
- `CSSAnimator` finishes when the clamped eased value reaches 0.9999, not when `duration` runs out: overshooting curves (`ease_out_back`, `ease_out_elastic`) end early, and `ease_in_circ`, `ease_in_bounce` and `triangular` can never finish.
- `Validation.is_number(Infinity)` is `true`, and numeric strings are not numbers.

See `docs/Utilities.md` for the full API.

---

## DevBridge

Dev only, not singletons — instantiate as needed. `DevBridge` keeps a WebSocket open to the ohzi-mcp server and runs each command through a registered handler. The other classes are what the handlers call: `SceneInspector`, `SceneEditor`, `CameraBridge`, `CaptureService`, `ConsoleBuffer`, `PerformanceProbe`, `InputSynthesizer`, `ViewNavigator`, `RenderModeRegistry`, `DebugDrawer` and `ModelLoader`. They take the singletons they read as arguments.

```ts
const bridge = new DevBridge();
const inspector = new SceneInspector();
const capture = new CaptureService(Graphics, () => CameraManager.current !== undefined);

bridge.register('inspect_scene', 'immediate', (args) => inspector.inspect(SceneManager.current, args));
bridge.register('capture_viewport', 'frame_end', (args) => capture.capture(args));
bridge.init({ port: 7317, app_info: () => app_info() });  // ws://127.0.0.1:7317

// In the application:
on_frame_end() { bridge.on_frame_end(); }                  // runs the queued frame_end commands
```

- Register anything that changes what renders as `frame_end`; reads and input gestures, which wait on real time, can be `immediate`.
- A handler's thrown error reaches the server with its `code` (`handler_failed` when it has none); an unknown command replies `unknown_command`. A closed socket retries every 2 s until `dispose()`.
- `PROTOCOL_VERSION` in `dev_bridge/protocol.ts` must match `mcp/src/protocol.ts`, or the server refuses the connection.
- `CameraBridge` moves the `CameraController` (tilt, orientation, azimuth in degrees, normalized `zoom`, `target`) when there is one, and refuses a raw `position` then (`controller_owns_camera`).
- `CaptureService` fast captures read the live canvas, which needs `preserveDrawingBuffer: true`, and cap the long edge at 1280 px (`max_size: 0` turns it off). Hires captures re-render through `Graphics.take_screenshot` up to 8192 px and need a camera.
- `RenderModeRegistry.create()` only builds the mode; pass it to `Graphics.set_state()`.
- `DebugDrawer.clear()` removes only the helpers it drew. `ModelLoader.load()` replaces a same-named direct child of the scene and keeps its transform.

See `docs/DevBridge.md` for the full API.

---

## Full Minimal Example

```ts
import {
  Initializer, Graphics, RenderLoop, BaseApplication,
  PerspectiveCamera, CameraManager, OScreen, SceneManager,
  NormalRender, Time, AbstractScene
} from '@ohzi/core';
import { WebGPURenderer, AmbientLight, Mesh, BoxGeometry, MeshStandardMaterial } from 'three';

// --- Scene ---
class MyScene extends AbstractScene
{
  constructor()
  {
    super({ name: 'main', compilators: { SceneCompilator, TexturesCompilator, AudiosCompilator } });
  }

  init()
  {
    super.init();
    const mesh = new Mesh(new BoxGeometry(), new MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x4488ff }));
    this.add(mesh);
    this.add(new AmbientLight(0xffffff, 1));
  }

  on_pre_render()
  {
    this.children[0].rotation.y += Time.dt;
  }
}

// --- Application ---
class App extends BaseApplication
{
  on_enter()
  {
    const scene = new MyScene();
    scene.init();
    SceneManager.current = scene;

    const cam = new PerspectiveCamera(60, OScreen.aspect_ratio, 0.1, 1000);
    cam.position.set(0, 1, 3);
    CameraManager.current = cam;

    Graphics.set_state(new NormalRender());
  }
}

// --- Bootstrap ---
const renderer = new WebGPURenderer({ antialias: true });
document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement);

Initializer.init(input);
Graphics.init({ renderer, core_attributes: {}, dpr: window.devicePixelRatio });

const app = new App();
const loop = new RenderLoop(app, Graphics, input);
loop.start();
```
